events.title: Ottoman Uyvar Eyalet
hints: A fortress town in the south-west fell in 1663 and became a provincial capital.
A Habsburg-led alliance recaptured it in 1685.
events.summary: In 1663 the Ottomans captured Nové Zámky and created the Uyvar Eyalet, which taxed much of south-western Slovakia. The Habsburgs retook the fortress in 1685.

events.title: Magyarization
hints: After 1867 the language of administration and schooling was imposed from Budapest.
Cultural institutions were closed in 1875 and a shooting in 1907 at Cernova became a symbol.
events.summary: After the Compromise of 1867, Hungarian authorities pursued policies of Magyarization, including the closure of Slovak-language secondary schools and the cultural society Matica slovenska in 1874–75. The 1907 Cernova shooting killed 15 villagers.

events.title: First Vienna Award
hints: Arbitrators from Berlin and Rome drew a new border in November 1938.
A fertile southern strip with Kosice was ceded.
events.summary: The First Vienna Award of November 1938, decided by Germany and Italy, transferred southern Slovakia and part of Carpathian Ruthenia to Hungary. The territories returned in 1945.

events.title: Slovak client state
hints: A republic declared in March 1939 under German 'protection'.
Tens of thousands of Jews were deported in 1942 under the regime's own laws.
events.summary: The Slovak Republic was proclaimed in March 1939 as a client state of Nazi Germany, which kept a protectorate over it. In 1942 the government deported about 58,000 Jews, and an uprising in 1944 was crushed by German troops.

events.title: Warsaw Pact invasion and occupation
hints: Soviet tanks rolled in during August 1968 to halt reforms.
Troops remained for more than two decades.
events.summary: Warsaw Pact forces led by the Soviet Union invaded in August 1968 to end the reforms of the Prague Spring. Soviet forces remained in the country until 1991.
